questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests release governance, least-privilege principles, and practical DevOps automation in AWS. It also evaluates the ability to translate business requirements into concrete infrastructure changes.

## Key Concepts
- CodePipeline stages and manual approval actions
- Stage-specific artifact storage using separate S3 buckets
- IAM role scoping for production deployments with guardrails

## Code Example
```yaml
Resources:
  ProdPipeline:
    Type: AWS::CodePipeline::Pipeline
    Properties:
      RoleArn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/CodePipelineServiceRole
      Stages:
        - Name: Source
          Actions:
            - Name: Source
              ActionTypeId:
                Category: Source
                Owner: ThirdParty
                Provider: GitHub
              Configuration:
                Owner: my-org
                Repo: my-repo
                Branch: main
              OutputArtifacts:
                - Name: SourceOutput
        
        - Name: Build
          Actions:
            - Name: Build
              ActionTypeId:
                Category: Build
                Owner: AWS
                Provider: CodeBuild
              InputArtifacts:
                - Name: SourceOutput
              OutputArtifacts:
                - Name: BuildOutput
              Configuration:
                ProjectName: MyBuildProject
        
        - Name: Deploy-Staging
          Actions:
            - Name: DeployStaging
              ActionTypeId:
                Category: Deploy
                Owner: AWS
                Provider: CloudFormation
              InputArtifacts:
                - Name: BuildOutput
              Configuration:
                StackName: my-app-staging
                TemplatePath: BuildOutput::template.yaml
                RoleArn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/CodePipelineDeployRole
              
        - Name: Manual-Approval
          Actions:
            - Name: ApproveProdDeploy
              ActionTypeId:
                Category: Approval
                Owner: AWS
                Provider: Manual
              Configuration:
                CustomData: "Please review and approve production deployment"
        
        - Name: Deploy-Production
          Actions:
            - Name: DeployProduction
              ActionTypeId:
                Category: Deploy
                Owner: AWS
                Provider: CloudFormation
              InputArtifacts:
                - Name: BuildOutput
              Configuration:
                StackName: my-app-prod
                TemplatePath: BuildOutput::template.yaml
                RoleArn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/CodePipelineProdRole
      ArtifactStore:
        Type: S3
        Location: !Ref ProductionArtifactsBucket
  
  StagingArtifactsBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      BucketName: my-app-staging-artifacts
      VersioningConfiguration:
        Status: Enabled
  
  ProductionArtifactsBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      BucketName: my-app-production-artifacts
      VersioningConfiguration:
        Status: Enabled
  
  CodePipelineProdRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: CodePipelineProdRole
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: codepipeline.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AWSCodePipelineFullAccess
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: ProductionDeployOnly
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - cloudformation:CreateStack
                  - cloudformation:UpdateStack
                  - cloudformation:DeleteStack
                  - cloudformation:DescribeStacks
                Resource: arn:aws:cloudformation:*:*:stack/my-app-prod/*
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - s3:GetObject
                  - s3:PutObject
                  - s3:ListBucket
                Resource:
                  - !GetAtt ProductionArtifactsBucket.Arn
                  - !Sub "${ProductionArtifactsBucket}/*"
              - Effect: Deny
                Action:
                  - cloudformation:CreateStack
                  - cloudformation:UpdateStack
                Resource: arn:aws:cloudformation:*:*:stack/my-app-staging/*
```

## Testing Steps
1. **Pipeline Creation**: Deploy the CloudFormation template and verify the pipeline appears in AWS Console
2. **Artifact Bucket Isolation**: Confirm staging artifacts don't appear in production bucket and vice-versa
3. **Manual Approval**: Trigger the pipeline and verify it stops at the manual approval stage
4. **IAM Guardrails**: Attempt to deploy to staging using the CodePipelineProdRole (should fail)
5. **Production Deployment**: Approve the manual step and verify successful production deployment
6. **Audit Trail**: Check CloudTrail logs for approval actions and deployment events

## Why Interviewers Ask This

This question checks if you understand:
- **Multi-account AWS architecture**: How to securely connect resources across different AWS accounts
- **Event-driven systems**: Using SQS and Lambda together for asynchronous processing
- **Reliability**: Handling failures gracefully with dead-letter queues
- **Safe deployments**: Rolling out changes gradually with automatic rollback

## Key Patterns Used

1. **Cross-account IAM roles**: Instead of sharing credentials, the Prod Lambda assumes a role in the Data account to get access

2. **Idempotency**: Using DynamoDB to track processed message IDs prevents duplicate work if the same message is delivered twice

3. **Dead-letter queue**: Failed messages don't disappear—they go to a DLQ so you can investigate and reprocess later

4. **Canary deployment**: Route a small percentage of traffic to the new version, watch for problems, then either rollback or full deploy

5. **Latency-based routing**: Route 53 sends users to the fastest responding endpoint—useful for cross-region canary testing

## Common Mistakes to Avoid
- Forgetting to check if a message was already processed (no idempotency)
- Not setting up a DLQ (lost messages = lost data)
- Rolling out to all users immediately without testing
- Not monitoring the right metrics for rollback decisions

## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of secure, auditable deployments and basic rollback mechanics in CodePipeline.

- Least-privilege IAM for Lambda execution role and CodePipeline

- Versioning and rollback of Lambda functions

## Code Example
```yaml
Resources:
  LambdaRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: "2012-10-17"
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal: { Service: "lambda.amazonaws.com" }
            Action: "sts:AssumeRole"
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: LambdaLoggingPolicy
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: "2012-10-17"
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogGroup
                  - logs:CreateLogStream
                  - logs:PutLogEvents
                Resource: "arn:aws:logs:*:*:*"
        - PolicyName: S3AccessPolicy
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: "2012-10-17"
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action: s3:GetObject
                Resource: "arn:aws:s3:::deployment-bucket/*"

  LambdaFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      Role: !GetAtt LambdaRole.Arn
      # ... other function properties

  ErrorAlarm:
    Type: AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm
    Properties:
      AlarmName: LambdaErrorAlarm
      AlarmDescription: "Triggers rollback on 5xx errors"
      MetricName: 5XXError
      Namespace: AWS/ApiGateway
      Statistic: Sum
      Period: 60
      EvaluationPeriods: 5
      Threshold: 10
      ComparisonOperator: GreaterThanThreshold
      AlarmActions:
        - !Ref RollbackAction

  RollbackAction:
    Type: AWS::CodePipeline::Action
    Properties:
      Configuration:
        ActionTypeId:
          Category: Invoke
          Owner: AWS
          Provider: Lambda
          Version: 1
      InputArtifacts: []
      Name: RollbackAction
      RunOrder: 2
```

## Testing Steps
1. Deploy the CloudFormation stack
2. Verify Lambda has only minimal IAM permissions
3. Test API Gateway access controls
4. Trigger 5xx errors to confirm CloudWatch alarm activation
5. Verify automatic rollback to previous Lambda version
